Import an Encrypted Export File as Case Data

Source: R/import_export_import.R
episodic_cases_import.Rd

Opens a file written by episodic_cases_export() at another instance, verifies it in full, and returns its cases as a validated data frame in the case data format. It does not write to the database: hand the result to episodic_run_cron() as imports, and the cases are loaded, deduplicated, detected on and recorded like every other case, with the import itself recorded against that run.

Usage

episodic_cases_import(
  file,
  key = Sys.getenv("EPISODIC_IMPORT_KEY", unset = NA),
  trusted_senders,
  passphrase = NULL,
  episodic_config_path = Sys.getenv("EPISODIC_CONFIG", unset = NA)
)

Arguments

file

The export file: a path, or its bytes as a raw vector.

key

Your secret encryption key, as its text or as the path of the file episodic_import_export_keygen() wrote. Defaults to the EPISODIC_IMPORT_KEY environment variable. Not used for a passphrase file.

trusted_senders

The public signing keys of the partners whose files you accept, each as its text or as the path of its .pub file. A file signed by any other key is refused.

passphrase

For a file written in passphrase mode: the passphrase. Leave NULL for a file encrypted to your key.

episodic_config_path

The configuration path, for the geography the warnings are measured against. Defaults to the EPISODIC_CONFIG environment variable.

Value

A data frame of class episodic_imported_cases, with exactly the case data columns, and the "import" attribute.

Details

partner <- episodic_cases_import(
  "partner.episodic",
  trusted_senders = "keys/partner_signing.pub"
)
episodic_run_cron(cases = my_cases, imports = partner)

Nothing in the file is returned unless all of it holds: it must open with your key (or the passphrase), its signature must verify against one of trusted_senders, and every table must match the SHA-256 its manifest records. A wrong key, an untrusted or forged sender, a tampered or truncated file, a format version this EpiSODIC does not read, and a hash mismatch each stop with an error that says which; a partially readable file is never partially imported. The error carries class episodic_import_export_error and a reason code.

What is returned:

  • source_key, patient_key and lab_number are prefixed with the sender's instance identifier and a colon, so the partner's keys can never be taken for yours.

  • institution_key is the stored hash the sender's database holds; the file declares it so, and the run uses it as it is.

  • A column the sender left out is NA on every row, which the case data format reads as "not recorded", never a default value.

  • Cases whose postcode this instance's reference data cannot place at some level are kept, with a warning per level.

The data frame carries class episodic_imported_cases and an "import" attribute describing the file (sender, signer fingerprint, range, omitted columns, the file's SHA-256, the warnings), which the run records.

Imports are append-only: a case the sender later corrects or retracts stays as it was first imported. See vignette("import-export") for this and the other limits (patient linkage across laboratories, pathogen naming, history imported after the first run).

See also

episodic_cases_export(), episodic_run_cron(), vignette("import-export")

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
partner <- episodic_cases_import(
  "partner.episodic",
  trusted_senders = "keys/partner_signing.pub"
)
attr(partner, "import")$omitted_fields
episodic_run_cron(cases = my_cases, imports = partner)
} # }
